taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts Coreopsis wrightii as a distinct species. Older ITIS/FNA treatments have synonymized it with Coreopsis basalis; the project follows current Kew while retaining the synonymy conflict in the learner.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — project Master Plant Pool records two wild Hays-local observations. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list includes Coreopsis wrightii. Mason — Mason Mountain WMA vascular flora includes a voucher for C. wrightii.
target_zone_range.guardrail: County evidence is exact; current Kew species concept retained despite older synonym treatments.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with life cycle, foliage, and ray pattern. Rock tickseed is an annual with narrow linear leaves and slender branching stems; the yellow ray florets usually carry rusty-red/brown color at the base.
diagnostic_traits: yellow ray florets with rusty-red to maroon basal markings

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with C. basalis, C. wrightii is generally narrower-leaved and often more slender, with the classic yellow rays carrying basal reddish-brown marks. Because older floras merge the taxa, final ID should use a full character set rather than ray color alone.
